records.rationale: Keyboard input is repeated across command guidance and benefits from one semantic, tokenized primitive.

evidence.accessibility: Uses the native kbd element and keeps key names as readable text.
evidence.performance: One inline element and token-only CSS.
evidence.ownership: Represents user input, not shortcut detection.
evidence.migration: Existing raw kbd markup can switch directly.

records.rationale: The expansion plan now freezes explicit locale, timezone, hydration-clock, formatter, and shared-scheduler ownership.

evidence.accessibility: Native time semantics retain a UTC-normalized machine-readable dateTime alongside visible localized output.
evidence.state: Relative timestamps use the supplied now for SSR and first hydration, then share interval subscriptions by refresh interval.
evidence.localization: Consumers explicitly provide locale and timezone; absolute presets and relative formatting behavior are frozen.
evidence.security: Values accept Date copies, finite epoch milliseconds, or complete offset-bearing timestamps only.
evidence.ssr: The supplied now anchors identical server and first-hydration output before elapsed client time is applied.
evidence.performance: One Tale scheduler groups subscribers by interval and the 1,000-timestamp tick vector is a maintained benchmark.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns validation, Intl formatting, hydration anchoring, and scheduling; applications own locale, timezone, and now.
evidence.migration: Applications can replace native time elements or app formatters with explicit absolute or relative Timestamp props.

records.rationale: The expansion plan approves a small semantic Root, Content, and Attribution composition with a strict cite boundary.

evidence.accessibility: Native blockquote, paragraph, and footer elements preserve quotation and attribution semantics.
evidence.localization: Quoted content and attribution remain consumer-authored.
evidence.security: Root cite accepts credential-free absolute HTTP(S) only; the parts expose no raw-HTML escape hatch.
evidence.ssr: The semantic part tree and validated cite attribute are deterministic.
evidence.performance: The composition adds no parser, observer, timer, or client state.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns semantic structure, styling, and cite validation while consumers own quotation content.
evidence.migration: Existing blockquote, paragraph, and footer markup maps directly to the three namespace parts.

records.rationale: The expansion plan now freezes atomic source normalization, shared ordinals, document identity, timestamps, and URL policy.

evidence.accessibility: References own stable targets and labels, unavailable sources are named, and the source list uses ordered-list semantics.
evidence.state: One immutable document-local registry normalizes atomically and repeated References share source-order ordinals.
evidence.localization: Source metadata remains consumer-authored while machine timestamps normalize to UTC independently of visible text.
evidence.security: Malformed, credential-bearing, unsupported, and unbased relative URLs lose their anchor while escaped metadata remains.
evidence.ssr: Normalized source order deterministically produces ordinals and Root-local entry IDs.
evidence.performance: Normalization builds one indexed source registry for repeated reference and list lookup.
evidence.ownership: Tale owns document identity, source normalization, numbering, list attributes, and URL policy.
evidence.migration: Existing Link-based references can move to explicit sources, references, and one ordered source list.

records.rationale: A plain-text, overflow-safe code surface is broadly useful while explicitly excluding highlighting and raw HTML.

evidence.accessibility: Uses pre/code semantics, preserves text, and allows an accessible label.
evidence.security: Accepts text children only; no raw HTML, Markdown, or syntax-highlighting execution.
evidence.performance: No parser or highlighter is bundled.
evidence.ownership: Presentation only; language tooling and execution are excluded.

records.rationale: KeyValuePairs already provides the same structured metadata-list role, so a second primitive would duplicate API and guidance.

evidence.accessibility: The existing component already supplies description-list semantics.
